A healthy stream sends bytes at least every 15 s: a frame, or a keepalive while the server waits for its next Postgres reconcile (web/src/server/desktop-cloud/run-stream.ts). Silence for twice that means something between the server and this reader holds or dropped the bytes.

Without this, a silent stream hid a running turn's output until the server's 120 s connection cap or the 150 s request timeout, since its viewer stops polling meanwhile.
entries.title: Shared/Core update: run-stream

ai.title: CloudRunReader watchdog stalls silent SSE streams after 30s idle
ai.summary: A watchdog mechanism was added to CloudRunReader in common/src/desktop-cloud/run-stream.ts to detect when an active Server-Sent Events stream stops sending data. The reader now tracks byte arrival and connection state, aborting the connection if it remains silent for 30000 ms, which is twice the server's 15-second keepalive interval. This change also introduced the CLOUD_STREAM_ID_HEADER constant to correlate logs between the server and the client, and a CloudStreamStall type to report diagnostic information about the stall when it occurs. Previously, a silent stream would remain connected until the server's 120-second cap or a 150-second request timeout expired, hiding a running turn's output from the viewer.
ai.evidence: The diff in common/src/desktop-cloud/run-stream.ts introduces CLOUD_STREAM_IDLE_MS, the CloudStreamStall type, and a watchdog timer in CloudRunReader that aborts silent SSE connections after 30 seconds and reports the stall via an onStall callback.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not indicate whether the onStall callback is currently wired to any user-facing telemetry or alerting system.

eli5.text: The Freebuff service now actively checks that live data streams are still sending updates, closing the connection and falling back to manual checks if a stream goes silent for thirty seconds. This safeguards the experience for anyone watching an AI task run in the desktop or web interface, preventing the screen from freezing while waiting for results. Previously, if the connection stalled, the output would remain hidden for several minutes until a longer timeout expired. The new safety check ensures the service notices the silence quickly and recovers, so you see the task's progress without long, unexplained gaps.

entries.title: CLI update: block-operations

acceptedPr.title: perf(cli): scan only the tag seam when appending stream text
acceptedPr.author: Salhi-zh
acceptedPr.body:
## What

The text streaming path in `cli/src/utils/block-operations.ts` concatenated the whole accumulated block with each incoming delta and then ran two `String.includes` scans over the result:

```ts
const combinedText = lastBlock.content + text
if (combinedText.includes(THINK_OPEN_TAG) || combinedText.includes(THINK_CLOSE_TAG)) { ... }
```

That made one reply cost **O(n²) in its own length** — every delta re-walked everything before it, allocating and flattening the concatenation each time.

## Why it's safe to narrow the scan

A think tag can only be *completed* by the delta that completes it, at the seam between the block's tail and that delta. A tag already sitting inside the block was split out when it arrived. So the check now:

1. looks at the last 7 characters of the block (the widest partial tag, `</think`), plus the delta itself;
2. falls back to the original full-block scan whenever either contains `<`.

`<` in ordinary prose (`a < b`) still takes the full path, so nothing is lost.

## Measurement (`bun`, same machine, before → after)

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 8,000 deltas, 470 KB, plain text | 434 ms | **1.1 ms** |
| 4,000 deltas, 234 KB | 117 ms | **0.9 ms** |
| 2,000 deltas, 117 KB | 34 ms | **0.7 ms** |
| 1,000 deltas, 59 KB | 21 ms | **0.4 ms** |
| 8 subagents × 600 deltas | 38 ms | **5.5 ms** |

Cost is now linear in stream length instead of quadratic (`us/delta` was rising 17 → 54 as the stream grew; it now sits flat below 0.5).

Memory: no leak found on this path. The batched updater's interval is already disposed when a turn ends (`use-send-message.ts`), so it was not changed.

## Verification

- **Behavioural equivalence, not just tests:** 432 corpus scenarios (18 texts × 12 chunk sizes, root and agent paths) dumped from both implementations — **byte-identical** output, sha256 `6e06dde1…`.
- `bun test src/utils src/hooks` — **2672 pass, 0 fail** (157 files).
- `bun run typecheck` — exit 0.
- New `block-operations-streaming.test.ts` covers tags split inside the tag syntax at every seam position, the 7-char `</think` boundary, and long blocks keeping every character.

One pre-existing quirk surfaced while writing the tests and is left untouched: `<think></think>` with no content emits zero blocks, and a tag arriving after a long prefix folds the prefix into the reasoning block. Both behave identically before and after this change, hence the narrower assertions in the new test file.

entries.summary: Agents, Shared/Core, Agent Runtime changes across 4 file(s) (+70/−14).

ai.title: Remove budget wording from base3 batching and no progress stop prompts
ai.summary: The base3 batching section and the no progress stop message no longer contain language that suggests cost constraints or limited session resources. The `BATCHING_GUIDANCE` constant in `agents/base3.ts` replaces its previous 'costs less' phrasing with an explicit instruction that batching is about fewer round trips and never about doing less. In `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/turn-progress.ts`, the `NO_PROGRESS_STOP_MESSAGE` removes the clause 'so carrying on would only spend your session' to prevent the model from interpreting the stop as a way to conserve credits. This change also adds `BASE3_BATCHING_STEP_PROMPT_PREVIOUS` in `common/src/constants/base3-step-prompt.ts` to help the server recognize older reminder texts sent by released clients.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies `agents/base3.ts` to remove the phrase 'costs less' from `BATCHING_GUIDANCE` and adds the line 'Batching is about fewer round trips, never about doing less', while `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/turn-progress.ts` removes the clause 'so carrying on would only spend your session' from `NO_PROGRESS_STOP_MESSAGE`.

changes.what: Updated `BATCHING_GUIDANCE` to remove cost-related language and explicitly state that batching is not about doing less work.
Modified `NO_PROGRESS_STOP_MESSAGE` to remove the reference to spending the session, addressing a model failure where it stopped early to save budget.
Added `BASE3_BATCHING_STEP_PROMPT_PREVIOUS` constant and updated `system-reminder.ts` to recognize older client reminder texts.

eli5.text: The assistant's instructions were updated to remove any wording that suggests cost or resource limits when batching work or stopping after periods of inactivity. This change affects developers who use the free coding assistant, ensuring the system does not internally signal that tasks should be cut short to save credits. In daily use, you will likely see the assistant complete requests more thoroughly instead of stopping early to conserve session resources, while the system remains compatible with older client versions that send previous reminder texts.
